card.name: Numeric cutoffs for triglyceride and lipid levels
card.fires_on: The space or comparison sign (≥, <) right before a number and mg/dL, in talk of triglyceride or fat levels. It marks where the lipid threshold value is about to appear.

modes.label: Space before lipid dose
modes.description: A blank space just before a mg amount in lipid or fat-emulsion text.

modes.label: Triglyceride threshold sign
modes.description: A ≥ or ( < sign before a number in triglyceride shift tables.
modes.example: (2/57) 9.6% (5/52) Fasting triglycerides Normal to High <150 to<< ≥>>200 (mg/dL)

modes.label: Level limit before mg/dL
modes.description: A space after words like below or above, before a triglyceride limit.
modes.example: Maintain triglyceride levels below<< >>400 mg/dL to reduce

card.writes: It slightly pushes away words about wax, soap and fatty or candle material, so the lipid number is read as a lab value.
card.plain: It fires just before a number in cholesterol or triglyceride cutoffs, such as 150 or 200 mg/dL.
